{{2012–13 Big East men's basketball standings}}

The '''2012–13 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Notre Dame]] in the sport of [[basketball]] during the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 college basketball season]].  The Fighting Irish competed in [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] of the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) and the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East Conference]]. They were led by head coach [[Mike Brey]], and played their home games at the [[Edmund P. Joyce Center]] [[Notre Dame, Indiana]].

==Previous season==
The Fighting Irish finished the 2011–12 season 22–12, 13–5 in Big East play, finishing third place behind Champion [[2011–12 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]].  There were several Irish to receive All-Big East honors.  Junior [[Jack Cooley]] was named the Big East's Most Improved as well as was named 2nd Team All-Big East.

The Irish were defeated in the semifinals of the [[2012 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] by Louisville. They earned a #7 seed for the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]],  where they were eliminated in the second round by [[2011–12 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]].

==Pre-season==

Following the end of the [[2011–12 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|2011–12 season]], both [[Tim Abromaitis]] and Scott Martin applied to the NCAA for a sixth year of eligibility. Abromaitis had been a redshirt during the [[2008–09 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|2008–09 season]], but suffered a torn ACL on November 25, 2011, during practice. He played in just two games during the season, having sat out the first four due to a misunderstanding of the rules during his redshirt season (he had played in exhibition games before the official start of the 2008–09 season).<ref>{{cite web|last=Fortuna|first=Matt|title=Tim Abromaitis not given 6th year|url=https://www.espn.com/chicago/ncb/story/_/id/7878959/tim-abromaitis-notre-dame-fighting-irish-denied-6th-year-elgibility|work=espn.com|date=May 2012|access-date=21 November 2012}}</ref>

Martin had transferred to Notre Dame after his freshman season at Purdue and sat out the 2008–2009 season due to NCAA transfer rules, but then suffered a torn ACL during a preseason practice in October 2009, causing him to miss a second full season. His petition for a sixth year was successful, but Abromaitis' was denied.<ref>{{cite web|title=Scott Martin Granted Sixth Year By NCAA|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/051112aab.html|work=und.com|accessdate=21 November 2012}}</ref>

In June 2012, Notre Dame officially announced a 10-year contract extension for head coach [[Mike Brey]], the third-winningest coach in school history<ref>{{cite web|title=Mike Brey Signs Contract Extension Through 2021-22 Season|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/061912aaa.html|work=und.com|accessdate=21 November 2012}}</ref>  and, with the retirement of [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]]'s [[Jim Calhoun]], now the second-longest tenured coach in the Big East after [[Jim Boeheim]].

Notre Dame recruited three players from the high school senior class of 2011–12, each of whom signed letters-of-intent in November 2011. The recruiting class was rated 16th in the nation by [[Rivals.com]]:<ref>{{cite web|title=Three Players Set To Join Notre Dame Men's Basketball Program|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/110911aab.html|work=und.com|accessdate=21 November 2012}}</ref>
